about: Curated by the Winger team (source: curated). Brand pairs in this catalogue whose names look or sound alike but contain different medicines. When a reading is matched to either name by approximation, or comes from handwriting or speech, the card is always amber and names both. Not an official list; add a pair only when both brands are in medicines.json and their salts differ.

pairs.why: Differ by two letters: rosuvastatin and atorvastatin are different statins at different doses.
Same opening sound: paracetamol and piroxicam (a painkiller of a different kind).
Same opening letters: escitalopram (for mood) and esomeprazole (for acidity).
Same shape when handwritten: losartan (blood pressure) and furosemide (water tablet).
Same opening sound: ramipril and carvedilol, two different heart medicines.
Same opening letters: atenolol (blood pressure) and atorvastatin (cholesterol).
